title: Tumbler: Puzzle Feedback Sound Effects
shortText: 101 puzzle SFX: 8 piece materials, each select, place, correct, wrong, nearly and undo, plus matches. WAV + OGG.
html:
Hear the move without looking at the screen

101 puzzle sound effects: 8 piece materials, and every one answers the same 6 ways: picked up, set down, correct, wrong, nearly right and taken back.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 26 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The wood block and the glass gem complete, every answer and every take, the "nearly" answer of the other 6 pieces, a match clearing for three to six pieces, the timer bed and a button.

Six answers, every piece

A puzzle player is looking at the board, not at the interface, so the sound has to say what a move did. Every piece here answers:

  • select: the piece picked up
  • place: two takes, the piece set down
  • correct: the move was right, a bright strike and a sparkle of its own material
  • wrong: the move was wrong, a dull low double knock
  • nearly: close, but not right, a strike that wobbles and is muffled
  • undo: the move taken back, a backward sweep and a tick

So you wire a piece once and only its material changes: wood_nearly, gem_nearly, marble_nearly. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: all 8 pieces carry exactly this chain, and the 120 pairs of answers inside each piece all differ.

The pieces

  • Wood block: a wooden block, a dry knock on the board.
  • Glass gem: a faceted glass gem, a bright clink.
  • Stone tile: a heavy stone tile, a low grind and thud.
  • Brass gear: a small brass gear, a metal tick that rings.
  • Clay tile: a glazed clay tile, a short ceramic tock.
  • Crystal shard: a crystal shard, a high ring that hangs in the air.
  • Jelly piece: a soft jelly piece, a wet squish and a bounce.
  • Marble: a glass marble, a roll and a click into place.

Around the pieces

  • 9 match and combo sounds: a match of three, four, five and six pieces clearing (each longer than the last), a combo building in four steps (each brighter than the last, never a rising tune) and a board clear. Measured: 6 steps across both ladders, failing steps: 0.
  • 13 board state sounds, the ones most packs leave out: a hint spent, locked until later, already tried, partial progress, solved, failed, reset and shuffle.
  • 11 move sounds: rotate, slide, swap and fall.
  • 12 time and interface sounds: timer ticks and a warning, a ticking timer bed and a quiet board bed (both loops), buttons, back, toggles and a star.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by piece and answer.
  • 2 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 18 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness, so the twentieth piece set down is not the first one again.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.91 dB, so a button tick and a board clear share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 922 checks, 0 failed.

Honest limits

These are synthesised, stylised sounds designed for games, not recordings. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. No cards (those live in a separate pack), no coins, no voices and nothing musical: a correct answer is a bright strike of the piece's own material, never a jingle.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Shuffle and Tell, the deckbuilder card table: draws, plays and shuffles for card puzzles.
  • Tally, clicker and idle feedback ladders.
  • Typeset, typewriter and handwriting text sounds for word puzzles.
